exposure: Suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection in pregnancy
cohort: The study recruited 8239 pregnant women who had suspected or confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection episodes between January 2020 and March 2021.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection during pregnancy was associated with indicated pre-term birth (most commonly for fetal compromise) and a significantly higher proportion of stillbirths in participants delivering within 2 weeks of infection, although overall birthweight, congenital malformations, and neonatal infection rates were largely unaffected or uncommon.
followup_time: Early neonatal period (first 7 days of life)
birth_weight: Birthweight, small for gestational age (SGA), and fetal growth restriction (FGR) were assessed.
gest_age: Gestational age was assessed to determine pre-term birth rates.
